# QC05: 清夏斋 Qingxia Zhai

Wave 4 · Qichun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=QC05` · Page: `/scenes/#QC05` · Row: `research/buildings/QC05-qingxia-zhai/`

## What it was

清夏斋 Qingxia Zhai, "Studio of Clear Summer", in the west of Qichun Yuan, two courts side by side on land with a long history: 裕亲王's 萼辉园 about 1687, then 交辉园, 春和园, and Prince Cheng's 西爽村 from 1773 to 1799 (E0626). West is 清夏斋, a seven-bay 工字 hall (palace_r7_halls; E0517, E0626); east is 延寿寺 (first 双寿寺, renamed 竹林院 by Jiaqing), front hall three bays, rear five (E0626). Jiaqing noted in 1804 that the old plaque here read 凤麟洲, given by Qianlong to Prince Cheng, before that name moved to the island QC06 (E0606). Poems of 1805-1824 show a study on a green pool with a stream, rocks, a small cascade, pines and bamboo, used in summer (E0624). A wine-cup pavilion (流杯亭) stood in it: square, 12 square column bases, about 48 stones, throne in the south half, cup stone in the north (E0628, E0629). From 1850 (or 1855, E0625) the residence of 如皇贵太妃 until her death in spring 1860 (E0624, E0625). Burned on 18 October 1860 (E0680).

From the inventory row: **built** by 1805 (first dated item); **changed** 同治十二年 1873 renamed 清夏堂; 1874 上梁 only (S220); 1850-1860 residence of 如皇贵太妃; plaque 凤麟洲 until 1804, then 清夏斋; 1870s repair planned, not done; **destroyed** 1860 (S06, S52, S01, S220, S360, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

In Jiaqing's 绮春园三十景: 清夏斋 and 竹林院 (the east court, later 延寿寺) (S223 卷十八; E0448). The same text says the few bays once named 凤麐洲 were renamed 清夏斋: 舊有數楹名鳳麐洲，後易名清夏齋 (S223; E0448), which agrees with Jiaqing's note of 1804 (E0606).

### How later sources differ

Renamed 清夏堂 in Tongzhi's edict of 1873 (E0434); six card models of the 1874 design survive in the Palace Museum (E0627): both after the target state, so they show the 1874 project, not 1860.

## What survives today

In about 2011 the sites of 清夏堂 (清夏斋) and 延寿寺 were occupied by other institutions (E1011). The stone seat of the wine-cup pavilion is said to survive (E0629).

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.
